summary: Extends the IMAP LIST command with attributes that identify special-use mailboxes such as drafts or sent mail, so clients do not have to ask users to configure them. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: Mail folders have jobs like drafts or sent. This lets the server label them so your email app finds the right ones.

questions: how does an imap client find the sent folder

how to create an imap drafts mailbox
subtitle: How an IMAP server can tell your mail client which folder is Drafts, Sent, Trash and so on.

tldr.problem: Mail clients let users choose where drafts and sent messages go, but setting that up means knowing which mailboxes the server has reserved for those jobs.
tldr.mechanism: The server adds optional special-use attributes such as \Drafts, \Sent and \Trash to IMAP LIST responses. An optional USE parameter on CREATE and an optional METADATA entry can also assign them.
tldr.outcome: A client can find the right mailboxes without asking the user. Support is optional, so a server may offer any combination of the attributes, or none.

today: RFC 6154 is a Proposed Standard, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Some IMAP message stores include special-use mailboxes, such as those that hold draft or sent messages. Many mail clients allow users to say where drafts and sent copies should be put, but configuring that requires knowing which mailboxes the server set aside.

This extension adds new optional mailbox attributes that a server may include in LIST responses to identify those mailboxes. It also adds an optional USE parameter on CREATE, so a client can assign a special use when it creates a mailbox. Servers may support that second part, but are not required to.
sections.eli5: Your email app needs to know which folder is for drafts and which is for sent mail. The server can now just tell it.

sections.title: The Special-Use Attributes
sections.content:
A server that supports the extension MAY include any of the new attributes in responses to the ordinary LIST command, next to existing ones such as \Marked and \Noselect. A mailbox can have none, one or several. The seven attributes are:

  • \All: presents all messages in the user's message store, almost certainly as a virtual mailbox.
  • \Archive: used to archive messages; the meaning is server-dependent.
  • \Drafts: holds messages being composed but not yet sent.
  • \Flagged: presents all messages marked as important.
  • \Junk: holds messages deemed to be junk mail.
  • \Sent: holds copies of sent messages.
  • \Trash: holds deleted or marked-for-deletion messages.

A special use can be advice to a client about what to put in the mailbox, or about what to expect to find there. All of the attributes are OPTIONAL. Special-use attributes are likely to be user-specific: if Adam shares his \Sent mailbox with Barb, it is unlikely to also be Barb's \Sent mailbox.
sections.eli5: It is like colored stickers on folders: one for drafts, one for sent mail, one for trash, and a few more. A folder can have no sticker, or more than one.

sections.title: Capabilities and the Extended LIST
sections.content:
There is no capability string for special-use attributes on the plain LIST command. For the extended list command from RFC 5258, the extension adds a capability string, a selection option and a return option, all called SPECIAL-USE.

  • A supporting server MUST include SPECIAL-USE in its CAPABILITY response.
  • With the selection option, LIST MUST return only mailboxes that have a special-use attribute.
  • With the return option, LIST MUST return the attributes on mailboxes that have them. The selection option implies the return option.

The server MAY return the attributes even when the client did not ask for the return option.
sections.eli5: The app can ask, 'Show me only the folders that have stickers,' or 'Show me everything, with stickers.' The server has to answer honestly.

sections.title: Setting a Use with CREATE
sections.content:
As an OPTIONAL feature, a server MAY let clients designate a mailbox, at creation, as having one or more special uses. The USE parameter on CREATE takes a parenthesized list of zero or more attributes. A server that supports this advertises CREATE-SPECIAL-USE, and clients MUST NOT use USE unless it does. This is a different capability string from SPECIAL-USE, and a server that supports both functions MUST advertise both.

Some special uses may cause side effects. Creating a \Junk mailbox might make the server start filing spam there, and creating an \All mailbox might produce a virtual mailbox where, for example, COPY into it might fail.

A server MAY allow a second mailbox with a use that already exists, which might move the use or create duplicates. It MAY instead refuse. If it cannot create the mailbox, it MUST NOT create it and MUST answer with a tagged NO. If the cause is the special-use attribute, the server SHOULD include the new USEATTR response code.
sections.eli5: When you make a new folder, you can ask for a sticker at the same time. If the server cannot do that, it says no and does not make the folder.

sections.title: Using IMAP METADATA
sections.content:
If a server supports this extension and the METADATA extension (RFC 5464), it SHOULD tie a mailbox's special-use attributes to the metadata entry /private/specialuse. Its value is NIL if there are none, or a space-separated list of attributes written as they appear in LIST responses.

Such a server MAY let clients change special uses through METADATA. It MUST check each change as strictly as it checks CREATE and its internal mechanisms. It MUST NOT blindly accept values that would set unsupported uses or produce duplicates the implementation considers invalid.
sections.eli5: The stickers can also be changed afterwards, but the server checks every change so nobody puts a sticker it cannot handle.

sections.title: Formal Syntax
sections.content:
The ABNF extends several rules from the base IMAP specification (RFC 3501), RFC 4466 and RFC 5258. A use-attr is one of the seven names above or a use-attr-ext, which is a backslash followed by an atom and is reserved for future extensions.

Clients MUST ignore list attributes they do not understand. Servers MUST NOT generate extension attributes except as defined by future Standards-Track revisions of or extensions to this specification.
sections.eli5: If the app sees a sticker it does not know, it ignores it. The server may not invent new stickers on its own.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Telling a client about special uses exposes a little extra information an attacker might value. Knowing which mailbox is \All, for example, points to every message the user has. This matters if the IMAP channel is not protected from passive eavesdropping.

For the USE parameter and metadata, implementors SHOULD consider letting a user designate the target of automatic server action. If a user could give \Junk to a shared mailbox, legitimate mail misclassified as junk would land there, exposing private mail to others. A server might warn the user or refuse the designation on a shared mailbox.
sections.eli5: Labels tell a snooper which folder holds everything, so keep the connection private. Also, do not let the junk label point at a folder other people can read.

items.label: All messages
items.desc: Presents all messages in the user's message store.

data.title: CREATE with the USE parameter
data.code:
C: t1 CAPABILITY
S: * CAPABILITY IMAP4rev1 CREATE-SPECIAL-USE
S: t1 OK done

C: t2 CREATE MySpecial (USE (\Drafts \Sent))
S: t2 OK MySpecial created

C: t3 CREATE Everything (USE (\All))
S: t3 NO [USEATTR] \All not supported
